label: sprites/fw_steam.spr: a steam puff that rises and thins, animated

R1.reason: Reads as a steam or smoke puff: a soft grey plume that builds from a bright base, rises, and thins into faint wisps by frames 12 to 15. It is the effect the brief asks for.

R2.reason: The frames are 64 by 64, the original's size, but the plume is a narrow column about 40 of the 64 units wide in most frames, sitting in the middle-left, and in frames 2 to 7 and 8 to 11 it runs to the top and bottom edges of the frame. Steam filling its frame as the class does is not met, so this is clearly off.

R3.reason: Neutral grey and off-white haze on a near-black ground, with a brighter base in frames 2 to 7. Nothing tinted or neon, and it suits a steam puff in the mod's palette. Judged by eye as the brief asks.

R4.reason: Measured against the smoke puff class: first frame 0.2 (range 0 to 0.35), peak at 0.2 (range 0.2 to 0.6), last frame 0 (range 0 to 0.1), jitter 1.48 (range 0.9 to 1.5), border 0.003 (range 0 to 0.005). All in range. Frames 0 to 1 are small, 2 to 7 grow and brighten, 8 to 15 thin and fade to dark. The count of 16 is the class's own, and the envelope ends dark as the class does.

R5.reason: The file is parallel and additive, read back at 64 by 64 with the name fw_steam.spr. The brief names no file to replace, so the type cannot be checked against one. But the amendment of 2026-10-16 says the game's steam1 is parallel oriented, and a steam puff built parallel failed R5 by measure there. Under the rubric's strict reading this is a fault until the type is confirmed against the file it stands in for.
